title: To posthumously award the Congressional Gold Medal, collectively, to Glen Doherty, Tyrone Woods, J. Christopher Stevens, and Sean Smith, in recognition of their contributions to the Nation.
official_summary:
This act directs the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate to arrange for the posthumous award of a Congressional Gold Medal to commemorate Glen Doherty, Tyrone Woods, J. Christopher Stevens, and Sean Smith, four Americans killed in the September 11, 2012, attack on the U.S. consulate in Benghazi, Libya. (Stevens was the U.S. Ambassador to Libya at the time, Smith was an officer in the Foreign Service, and Doherty and Woods were both government contractors and former Navy SEALs.)

After the medal has been awarded, it shall be given to the Central Intelligence Agency Museum.

summary.headline: Directs Congress to posthumously award Congressional Gold Medals to four Americans killed in the 2012 Benghazi consulate attack, and then give the medal to the CIA Museum.
summary.what_it_does: This law directs the House Speaker and the Senate President pro tempore to arrange a posthumous Congressional Gold Medal honoring Glen Doherty, Tyrone Woods, J. Christopher Stevens, and Sean Smith. The four men died in the September 11, 2012, attack on the U.S. consulate in Benghazi, Libya. Stevens was the U.S. Ambassador to Libya, Smith was a Foreign Service officer, and Doherty and Woods were government contractors and former Navy SEALs. After the medal is awarded, it goes to the Central Intelligence Agency Museum.
summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 21, 2022; the summary does not list a separate effective date.
